hints.title: Recursive Anchor Initialization
hints.text: Locate the root record where manager_id is null to retrieve the chief executive salary and seed level one with direct reports.

hints.title: Recursive Traversal
hints.text: Join the previous recursive hierarchy set with employees where manager_id matches preceding subordinates, incrementing the hierarchy level.

hints.title: Salary Difference and Ordering
hints.text: Subtract the chief executive base salary from each subordinate salary. Sort rows primarily by hierarchy level ascending and secondarily by subordinate id ascending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE Subordinates AS (
    SELECT
        e.employee_id AS subordinate_id,
        e.employee_name AS subordinate_name,
        1 AS hierarchy_level,
        e.salary - ceo.salary AS salary_difference
    FROM Employees e
    JOIN Employees ceo ON ceo.manager_id IS NULL
    WHERE e.manager_id = ceo.employee_id
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT
        e.employee_id,
        e.employee_name,
        s.hierarchy_level + 1,
        e.salary - ceo.salary
    FROM Employees e
    JOIN Subordinates s ON e.manager_id = s.subordinate_id
    JOIN Employees ceo ON ceo.manager_id IS NULL
)
SELECT
    subordinate_id,
    subordinate_name,
    hierarchy_level,
    salary_difference
FROM Subordinates
ORDER BY hierarchy_level ASC, subordinate_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Recursive CTE traverses hierarchy tree layer by layer.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Static self-joins cannot handle arbitrary organizational depth.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Linear intermediate table stores discovered subordinates.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Implements recursive CTE with level tracking and root baseline subtraction.
